title: Choose how a studio links its design tools, asset library and social accounts
scenario: The studio will link a design tool, a brand library and a social account to its own AI app through MCP. You decide how, before the launch. Use the exhibit. The names, folders, tools and numbers are made up for this case. The vendor lines are copied from the docs.
exhibit:
BRIEF:
  Marlow Bakery, autumn launch. The studio wants its own AI app, "Marlow
  Helper", to read the design file, use the brand library, and help post the
  final ad on Friday at 18:00. Everything is linked through MCP servers.

DESIGN TOOL (made up for this case):
  Figma, through its remote MCP server. Marlow Helper was built by the studio.

LIBRARY (made up for this case):
  A library server run by the library vendor, on public HTTPS.
  Folders: PUBLIC, CLIENT-APPROVED, EMBARGOED (next season, unreleased).
  The master logo is replaced every quarter.
  Studio rule: no AI vendor may keep a copy of EMBARGOED files.
  The studio calls the library through the Claude API MCP connector.

SOCIAL (made up for this case):
  A scheduler server run by the scheduler company. Tools: list_comments,
  create_draft_post, publish_post. The studio has used the test account only.

KEYS (made up for this case):
  One OpenAI project key serves the moodboard server and the scheduler flow.
  It expires in 5 days.

NEXT YEAR (made up for this case):
  The client may ask the studio to move the set-up to another AI vendor.

VENDOR LINES (copied from the docs):
  Figma: "Only clients listed in the Figma MCP Catalog can connect to the Figma
  MCP Server."
  Claude, MCP connector: "The MCP connector is not covered by ZDR arrangements."

questions.prompt: Before planning to connect Marlow Helper to Figma's server, what do you check first?

options.text: Nothing, because MCP is open, so any AI app can connect to any MCP server at all
options.explanation: The Figma docs say only clients listed in Figma's MCP Catalog can connect to Figma's server.

options.text: Whether Marlow Helper is in the Figma MCP Catalog, since only listed clients can connect
options.explanation: Right. This is Figma's own rule for its own server. A new client can join its waitlist.

options.text: Whether the server is local, because Figma's server only works on the designer's laptop
options.explanation: The Figma docs recommend Figma's remote server. They do not say the server is only local.

options.text: Whether Marlow Helper speaks SSE only, because that is the one transport Figma accepts
options.explanation: The Figma page does not name SSE as its rule. The catalog is the stated limit.

questions.prompt: The master logo changes every quarter. Which plan gives the app the current logo with the least upkeep?

options.text: Copy the three folders into a vendor's file store every quarter, so the AI reads fixed copies
options.explanation: A copy goes stale between quarters, and a copy of EMBARGOED sits at a vendor.

options.text: Link all three folders, because zero data retention covers everything the connector sends
options.explanation: The Claude docs say the MCP connector is not covered by ZDR arrangements.

options.text: Link all three folders, and ask the library vendor to promise that it will delete EMBARGOED
options.explanation: A promise is not a check. The studio rule is that no AI vendor keeps a copy.

options.text: Link PUBLIC and CLIENT-APPROVED through the server, and keep EMBARGOED out of the link
options.explanation: Right. A link returns the current logo with no re-copying. EMBARGOED stays out because the Claude connector is not ZDR-covered.

questions.prompt: Before publish_post is switched on for the live account, what must be ready?

options.text: An owner, the scopes and data allowed, the effects of a post, and a way to take it down
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI's guide lists these checks before write actions: owner, scopes, data access, external effects and a recovery path.

options.text: Only a good caption, because the AI app checks the rest of the posting rules by itself
options.explanation: Nothing in the cited pages says the app checks these. The studio has to prepare them.

options.text: Only a larger spend limit, because publishing costs tokens and the flow may run out of them
options.explanation: A spend limit is not the check that matters before a write to a live account.

options.text: Nothing more, because the test account worked and the live account has the same rules
options.explanation: A test does not cover the live account's scopes or its effects. Plan the recovery path first.

questions.prompt: The OpenAI project key expires in 5 days. What is the safe order of steps?

options.text: Revoke the old key, then create a new one, and update the apps when the team has time
options.explanation: Revoking first breaks every app that still uses the old key.

options.text: Create a new key, revoke the old key at once, and then update the apps that stopped
options.explanation: This causes a gap. Apps fail until they are updated.

options.text: Create a new key, update both apps, check that they work, then revoke the old key
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say to create a replacement, update your applications, and revoke the old key once the replacement is verified.

options.text: Wait for the key to expire, because an expired key is replaced by OpenAI on its own
options.explanation: The page says to rotate before expiry. It does not describe automatic replacement.

questions.prompt: Which set-up keeps a move to another AI vendor cheapest next year?

options.text: Standard remote servers, a connection sheet kept by the studio, and masters in studio storage
options.explanation: Right. The server moves between vendors, while the wrapper does not. The sheet and the masters stay in the studio's hands.

options.text: Each vendor's built-in connectors, because they are the most tightly joined to that vendor
options.explanation: Built-in connectors are the part that is stuck to one vendor. connector_id is even deprecated for new models.

options.text: One vendor's file store for masters, plus a beta feature that only that vendor offers
options.explanation: Both tie the studio to one vendor. Betas can also change or end.

options.text: A fresh set-up for each vendor, with nothing written down, so that nothing is ever shared
options.explanation: This repeats all the work and leaves no record. A shared sheet is the cheap part.
